signatures.name: EVERY ROAD
signatures.fantasy: You have walked all of it, and the more of it you are carrying at once, the more the road gives back.
signatures.baseMechanic: All your damage +20%, and +20% more for each OTHER skill that has already acted this wave. Holds 6s.
signatures.dials: AmplifyPercent 0.20 (SoloBattle:1747 ampBonus), AmplifyMs 6000 (:1728 window), AmplifyWholeWave true (:1748), Effect Amplify (:1722), Beats 5 (:1661), Targets 1. NEW AmplifyPerSkillUsed 0.20 — read ONCE, in the Sign cast branch just after ampBonus is set (:1749): ampBonus += def.AmplifyPerSkillUsed * Math.Max(0, activated.Count - 1). `activated` already exists (:725, SPIRIT/HARMONY) and already counts Field pulses and Reaction-free casts, so a broad weave is counted honestly.
signatures.whyItFits: The starter is the only champion with Lean = null and the only passive in the roster that is deliberately never wrong. Its signature is the one skill whose value is BREADTH rather than depth — the wanderer's actual claim, stated as a number.
signatures.innateInteraction: EVEN HAND is HitSize 1.08, and HitSize is read at SoloBattle:998, BEHIND the `if (skillDef is null) return m;` gate — so the innate lifts every SKILL by 8% and never once touches the champion's basic swing, which is about a third of a build's damage. The amplify window is read at :961, ABOVE that gate, so it is the only multiplier in the game that reaches the swing. EVERY ROAD is therefore the exact complement of the innate: the innate pays the half the swing cannot have, the signature pays the half the innate cannot reach. And because the innate is flat across styles, it is the one champion for whom weaving four unrelated skills costs nothing — which is precisely what this skill pays for.

variations.name: WAYFARING
variations.line: No burst. Each cast adds +15% for the rest of the wave, up to +60%, and the per-skill bonus falls to 12%.
variations.dials: AmplifyPercent 0 → AmplifyPerCast 0.15, AmplifyCap 0.60 (SoloBattle:1732-1744, the STEADY path, which sets window = TickCeilingMs), AmplifyPerSkillUsed 0.12

reinforcements.name: PACED
reinforcements.line: Each other skill that has acted is worth 20% instead of 12%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: the standing amplifier is deeper for the whole wave from the moment the second skill acts. Dead on CROSSROADS, which sets AmplifyPerSkillUsed to 0.

reinforcements.name: WELL TROD
reinforcements.line: Each cast adds 25% instead of 15%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: the swell reaches its cap in three casts instead of four. Dead on CROSSROADS, which has AmplifyPerCast 0.

reinforcements.name: HORIZON
reinforcements.line: The cap rises from +60% to +130%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt in the deep regions, where waves run long enough to cast five or six times. Dead on CROSSROADS, which has AmplifyCap 0.

variations.name: CROSSROADS
variations.line: It empowers the next 4 damaging hits at +150% instead, and stops counting your other skills.
variations.dials: AmplifyPercent 1.50, AmplifyMs 600000 (held until spent, the SPEND pattern), Rules.AmplifyHits 4 (SoloBattle:968-977, :1752-1753), AmplifyPerSkillUsed 0.20 → 0

reinforcements.name: FOUR WINDS
reinforcements.line: It empowers 7 hits instead of 4.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt, sharply in the shallow scenario where the partner is SPRAY and five arrows land per cast. Dead on WAYFARING, whose AmplifyHits is 0 (an uncounted window).

reinforcements.name: OVERLAND
reinforcements.line: Each empowered hit lands +230% instead of +150%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt on every empowered hit. Dead on WAYFARING, which sets AmplifyPercent to 0 and runs on the per-cast swell instead.

reinforcements.name: CLEAN SLATE
reinforcements.line: A critical hit is empowered without spending one of them.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: the charge drains at (1 - critChance) per hit, so the window covers more hits. Structurally dead on WAYFARING — the code path at :968 only runs when ampHitsLeft > 0, and WAYFARING never sets a count.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "mark", FxKey "mark". Every character already ships fx_{id}_mark_strip8_512 (assets/art/VFX/), so HuntScreen.FxFor picks up the Seeker's own strip with no new art. It should read as a road-sign or waypost struck into the ground in front of the champion, brightening one notch for each skill that has spoken this wave — the mark literally counting the weave.

signatures.name: OVERFALL
signatures.fantasy: You do not aim. You drop the whole weight on the whole room and let the arithmetic sort it out.
signatures.baseMechanic: Very heavy damage to EVERY enemy, every 6 beats.
signatures.dials: Beats 6 (SoloBattle:1661), Targets WholeWave (:1940 spreadTargets → :1314 LandSpread loop), BasePower 430 (:1818 PoweredBase), ClipKey/FxKey "strike". Deliberately sets NO OverkillCarry of its own.
signatures.whyItFits: THE ANVIL "hits things until they are a different shape", and its class weakness is stated in its own roster comment: an enormous hit on a small creature throws most of itself away. OVERFALL is that weakness made deliberate — it throws away more than any skill in the game, on purpose.
signatures.innateInteraction: This is the brief's own §5 example, taken literally. DEADWEIGHT is OverkillCarry 0.33, and SoloBattle:1271 reads `MathF.Max(shape.OverkillCarry, castCarry)` — the innate and a skill's own carry do NOT stack; the larger wins. So any signature that raised the carry would be arithmetically wasted below 0.33, and a signature that carried MORE would just be a bigger version of the passive. OVERFALL manufactures the overkill instead. One cast lands a 430-base blow on all five creatures of a Swarm at once, so a crowded wave produces four or five spills in the same instant, and the Anvil is the only champion in the roster that collects any of them (the carry at :1274 fires once per kill, one level deep). On any other champion the identical cast is the most wasteful skill in the catalogue.

variations.name: SHEER
variations.line: All of the weight falls on one enemy instead.
variations.dials: Targets WholeWave → 1, DamageMultiplier 1.0 → 2.6 (SoloBattle:1904)

reinforcements.name: PLUMB
reinforcements.line: Defence ignore: the blow ignores the target's defence.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt against the armoured bands — flat armour is subtracted per hit at :1180, and one huge hit that skips it is the largest single delta in the fixture.

reinforcements.name: TRUE LINE
reinforcements.line: After the blow, your next basic attack ignores defence too.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: the swing that follows the cast lands past armour instead of at the 15% floor.

reinforcements.name: HEADSTONE
reinforcements.line: The blow also kills the weakest enemy under 20% health, once a wave.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt and creatures killed. Worth nothing on LANDSLIDE by construction: the wave-wide blow has already killed everything under 20%, so the execute scan at :2003 finds no candidate.

variations.name: LANDSLIDE
variations.line: The weight falls on every enemy TWICE, at 70% each.
variations.dials: HitsPerTarget 1 → 2 (SoloBattle:1322-1341, and :1977 hitsPerTarget), DamageMultiplier 1.0 → 0.70

reinforcements.name: SECOND FALL
reinforcements.line: Three falls instead of two.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt, and far more overkill spilled per wave. Structurally dead on SHEER, which keeps HitsPerTarget at 1.

reinforcements.name: SCREE
reinforcements.line: If an enemy dies, the falls it had left drive into the next enemy.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt against thin waves — the `pending` counter at :1343 only exists when want > 1, so it is structurally inert on SHEER's single fall.

reinforcements.name: RUBBLE
reinforcements.line: Against a thin wave the falls double up: never fewer than 6 in all.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt against a one- or two-creature wave, where alive < 6 raises hitsPerTarget. Its whole point is a wave OVERFALL has already thinned, which is the state SHEER never produces.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "strike", FxKey "strike" — fx_anvil_strike_strip8_512 already exists. The cast should read as one drop rather than a swing: the effect lands simultaneously on every creature rectangle (HuntScreen's default ClipKey branch already sizes the flash to the creature being hit), with the SPILL drawn as a short low shockwave running from each corpse into the next living creature — the visual the innate has never had.

signatures.name: GRAVE SONG
signatures.fantasy: The charms do not stop singing when something dies. They get louder.
signatures.baseMechanic: Damages every enemy every 2s, and deals +35% more for each enemy the wave has already lost.
signatures.dials: Kind Field with IntervalMs 2000 (SoloBattle:1472 ownTick), Targets WholeWave, BasePower 16 per second (:1640, scaled by IntervalMs/1000). NEW DamagePerDeadEnemy 0.35 — read ONCE, in Amp() immediately beside SWARMBANE (SoloBattle:1029): `if (skillDef?.DamagePerDeadEnemy > 0f) m *= 1f + skillDef.DamagePerDeadEnemy * deadThisWave;`. `deadThisWave` already exists (:714, :1229, FIELD/REMNANT). One site serves the aura path, the cast path and the trap path alike.
signatures.whyItFits: MANY MOUTHS is the crowd passive, and a passive that scales with the crowd has one shape of problem: it is at its strongest the instant the wave lands and is worth nothing by the time the wave is nearly clear. THE CHORUS's own signature is the other end of the same wave.
signatures.innateInteraction: MANY MOUTHS is PerCreatureBonus 0.05, read at SoloBattle:1029 off `alive`. GRAVE SONG is read on the very next line off `deadThisWave` — the exact mirror, and `alive + deadThisWave` is the number the wave opened with. That makes the sum roughly constant and the SHAPE of it a decision: kill the front of a five-creature wave fast and the song is already at +140% while the mouths have collapsed to +5%; hold the crowd alive with spread damage and the mouths pay +25% while the song pays nothing. Two opposed clocks on the same wave, which is exactly what the brief asks for — a crowded wave becomes a choice instead of a bonus. It is emphatically not "+more damage per living enemy".

variations.name: KEENING
variations.line: The song stops counting the dead. It slows every enemy 25% instead, deepening 5% a pulse to 55%.
variations.dials: DamagePerDeadEnemy 0.35 → 0, SlowFraction 0.25, SlowDeepenPerTick 0.05, SlowCeiling 0.55 (SoloBattle:1557-1581, and the slow branch has NO continue, so the field still deals its tick)

reinforcements.name: LAMENT
reinforcements.line: The slow deepens 9% a pulse instead of 5%.
reinforcements.liveness: Health kept: the bite interval at :2169 is stretched by slowFactor, so fewer bites land per wave. Structurally dead on REQUIEM, which sets SlowFraction and SlowDeepenPerTick to nothing.

reinforcements.name: MOURNING
reinforcements.line: The ceiling rises from 55% to 75%.
reinforcements.liveness: Health kept in the long deep-region waves, where the slow reaches its ceiling. Dead on REQUIEM.

reinforcements.name: CHOIR
reinforcements.line: The slow starts at 40% instead of 25%.
reinforcements.liveness: Health kept from the very first pulse, which is where a wave that ends in four exchanges needs it. Dead on REQUIEM.

variations.name: REQUIEM
variations.line: The song comes half as often, twice as heavy, and the dead count double.
variations.dials: IntervalMs 2000 → 4000, DamageMultiplier 1.0 → 2.2 (SoloBattle:1643), DamagePerDeadEnemy 0.35 → 0.70

reinforcements.name: DIRGE
reinforcements.line: Each enemy the wave has lost is worth 110% instead of 70%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt, growing through the wave. Structurally dead on KEENING, which zeroes DamagePerDeadEnemy.

reinforcements.name: TOLLING
reinforcements.line: The song comes every 3s instead of every 4s.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: more pulses at the deep end of the wave, where the dead multiplier is largest. Worth nothing to KEENING, whose purchase is the slow's DEPTH per pulse — a faster clock there would only reach the same ceiling sooner.

reinforcements.name: PALL
reinforcements.line: The song deals 3.4x its weight instead of 2.2x.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt on every pulse. Aimed at the branch that has no control to fall back on.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "aura", FxKey "aura" (the one shared strip that already resolves). Draw it as charm-light hanging in the air ABOVE each corpse's last position rather than on the champion: the wave's dead should visibly accumulate as standing motes, so the player can literally count what the multiplier is reading. That also gives the Chorus the one thing its passive never had — a picture.

signatures.name: CADENCE
signatures.fantasy: You keep time whether or not anything is happening, and everything you own arrives sooner because of it.
signatures.baseMechanic: A shot at the front enemy every 1s, and every skill you own comes back 12% sooner.
signatures.dials: Kind Field, IntervalMs 1000 (SoloBattle:1472), Targets 1, BasePower 14 per second (:1640). NEW SkillRateBonus 0.12 — hoisted once from the woven skills beside `bleedRate`/`swingIgnoresArmour` (SoloBattle:749-768) and added as one term inside RateNow() (:856): `* (1f + skillRateFromSkills)`. One read site, and RateNow is already the single place every cadence in the fight is asked for.
signatures.whyItFits: "Keeps time. The fight is what happens between the beats." The Metronome is the only champion whose passive is about WHEN rather than how hard, and cooldown reduction is VOLLEY's owned verb (design §6), so the ownership table is respected.
signatures.innateInteraction: FIRST BEAT is two front-loaded gifts and nothing else: FreeOpeningCast (SoloBattle:1683 — openingBeat becomes 0) spends itself on the wave's very first action, and FirstHitMultiplier 2f (:1018) spends itself the first time each creature is touched. Both are gone inside the opening seconds, after which the Metronome is an ordinary champion for the rest of a 6-15 second wave. CADENCE owns exactly the half the innate cannot: it pays nothing at all at the opening — a rate bonus has nothing to accelerate on beat one — and compounds every second afterwards. It is also a Field, so it never competes with the free opening cast for the beat the innate just handed over. The two halves of the wave, split between passive and signature.

variations.name: SUBDIVISION
variations.line: The shot comes every 0.5s at half weight, and the rate bonus rises to 18%.
variations.dials: IntervalMs 1000 → 500, SkillRateBonus 0.12 → 0.18 (the aura's per-second BasePower is scaled by IntervalMs/1000 at :1642, so halving the clock halves each shot and holds the damage per second)

reinforcements.name: SIXTEENTHS
reinforcements.line: The shot comes every 0.3s.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: more separate hits, which is a real trade against flat armour (:1180 subtracts per hit) and a real gain for every per-hit rule. Worthless to HALF TIME, whose entire purchase is one heavy pulse that pays armour once.

reinforcements.name: DRIVING
reinforcements.line: Your skills come back 26% sooner instead of 18%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: BeatFor(RateNow()) at :2132 shortens the beat, so more casts land per wave. Structurally dead on HALF TIME, which sets SkillRateBonus to 0.

reinforcements.name: ACCENT
reinforcements.line: Each shot deals 90% of its weight instead of 50%.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt on every pulse. Sized to the fast branch's own weight, which HALF TIME does not have.

variations.name: HALF TIME
variations.line: No rate bonus. The shot comes every 3s, reaches every enemy, and lands far heavier.
variations.dials: SkillRateBonus 0.12 → 0, IntervalMs 1000 → 3000, Targets 1 → WholeWave, DamageMultiplier 1.0 → 2.4

reinforcements.name: AUGMENTED
reinforcements.line: The pulse lands at 3.6x its weight instead of 2.4x.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt across the whole wave every 3s.

reinforcements.name: FERMATA
reinforcements.line: The pulse comes every 2s instead of every 3s.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt. Worthless to SUBDIVISION, which is already at a half-second clock and is buying hit COUNT rather than pulse size.

reinforcements.name: RESOUNDING
reinforcements.line: The pulse hits an enemy under half health 70% harder.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt and creatures killed once a wave-wide pulse has chipped everything below half — a state a single-target stream never produces.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "projectile", FxKey "projectile" — fx_metronome_projectile_strip8_512 exists, and HuntScreen:1594 already flies a projectile across the gap and scales it to the distance. The shot should be a single small tick-mark bolt on a visibly regular clock, and the rate bonus should show as the skill rail's refill sweep running visibly faster (HuntScreen.RailCooldownMs) rather than as a second effect.

signatures.name: HOLD FAST
signatures.fantasy: Something is always being put back between you and the next thing that wants you dead.
signatures.baseMechanic: Every 2s you gain SHIELD worth 2.5% of your maximum health.
signatures.dials: Kind Field, IntervalMs 2000 (SoloBattle:1472), Targets 1, BasePower 0. NEW ShieldPerPulse 0.025 — read ONCE, in the Field block immediately after the Aura event is emitted (SoloBattle:1486-1490): `if (def.ShieldPerPulse > 0f || def.HealPerPulse > 0f) { GrantShield(champ.MaxHealth * def.ShieldPerPulse, ms); Heal(...); continue; }`. GrantShield (:820) already enforces the one cap, emits the one event and reports what was actually added.
signatures.whyItFits: "Has been killed. Declined." The Bulwark's whole claim is that the fight is not over when it should be, and SHIELD is the only resource in the game that is not health (ShieldRules, SoloBattle:31-38).
signatures.innateInteraction: SECOND WIND grants BuildTrigger.Undying, spent at SoloBattle:2399-2411: one killing blow per EXPEDITION is refused and the champion is left at Health = 1. At 1 health every subsequent bite is lethal, so as it stands the catch buys about one and a half seconds — the innate is a death save that hands you a position you cannot hold. HOLD FAST is the only thing in the roster that makes that position survivable, because AbsorbWithShield (:115, :2293) eats the bite BEFORE any of it reaches the pool, and nothing that reads Health reads shield. So a champion at 1 health with a standing shield is a champion still fighting, and the shield rebuilds itself every 2s while it fights. It is not a second death save and it is not more health: it is the resource that makes the innate's one refusal into a recovery. On any champion without UNDYING it is a modest, always-on mitigation.

variations.name: BREASTWORK
variations.line: The wall is built before the wave: every wave begins with SHIELD worth 15% of your maximum health, and the pulse falls to 0.8%.
variations.dials: WaveStartShieldFraction 0 → 0.15 (SoloBattle:831-833, granted after the wave's shield reset), ShieldPerPulse 0.025 → 0.008

reinforcements.name: REDOUBT
reinforcements.line: The wave begins with 26% instead of 15%.
reinforcements.liveness: Shield gained (the fixture reads ShieldGained events directly) and health kept in the opening exchange of every wave. Structurally dead on DEEP ROOTS, which never sets WaveStartShieldFraction.

reinforcements.name: FOOTINGS
reinforcements.line: The pulse returns to 2% instead of 0.8%.
reinforcements.liveness: Shield gained across a long wave, once the wave-start wall has been eaten.

reinforcements.name: QUICKLIME
reinforcements.line: The wall is rebuilt every 1s instead of every 2s.
reinforcements.liveness: Shield gained: twice the pulses. Worthless to DEEP ROOTS, whose heal is already bounded by the per-wave healing ceiling (:1404) rather than by how often it pulses.

variations.name: DEEP ROOTS
variations.line: Half the wall. Each pulse also heals 1% of your maximum health, and you can be healed 30% more each wave.
variations.dials: ShieldPerPulse 0.025 → 0.012, HealPerPulse 0 → 0.010 (read at the same new site, so a Field can heal without carrying an attack break), Rules.HealCeilingBonus 0.30 (SoloBattle:792-794)

reinforcements.name: WELLSPRING
reinforcements.line: Each pulse heals 1.8% instead of 1%.
reinforcements.liveness: Healing published (the fixture reads Heal events) and health kept in the deepest region, where the champion starts at half its pool. Structurally dead on BREASTWORK, which has HealPerPulse 0.

reinforcements.name: OVERFLOW
reinforcements.line: You can be healed 80% more each wave instead of 30%.
reinforcements.liveness: Healing published: without the room the bigger pulse is not a bigger pulse — this is the same repair BALM already needed. Dead on BREASTWORK, which heals nothing.

reinforcements.name: TAPROOT
reinforcements.line: The pulse comes every 1s instead of every 2s.
reinforcements.liveness: Healing published — twice the pulses is what makes the widened ceiling reachable inside one wave, which is the whole point of this branch and no part of the other.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "trap", FxKey "trap" — fx_unbroken_trap_strip8_512 exists. The pulse should read as a plate being set, not as a heal: a short hard flash at the champion's chest anchor on the same clock as the Aura event, and the existing shield bar and steel outline (BattleEventKind.ShieldGained / Undying) carry the rest. It must look like something being placed IN FRONT of the champion, never like light going into them, or it will read as healing and the whole distinction ShieldRules exists to protect is lost.

signatures.name: SLOW FALL
signatures.fantasy: You are not throwing anything. It is already falling, and it keeps arriving.
signatures.baseMechanic: A stone falls on the front enemy every 3s. It never takes your action.
signatures.dials: Kind Field, IntervalMs 3000 (SoloBattle:1472 ownTick), Targets 1, BasePower 42 per second → 126 per stone before resonance (:1640-1643, scaled by IntervalMs/1000). Beats 0, so it costs no beat by construction (SkillKind.Field, :1459).
signatures.whyItFits: "Slow. Arrives anyway." A tower does not swing; it comes down on its own schedule whatever the champion is doing. A HAMMER Field that lands real hits — as opposed to PRESS, which lands none — is a slot the catalogue does not have.
signatures.innateInteraction: MOMENTUM is FirstHitMultiplier 0.85 and LaterHitMultiplier 1.35, read at SoloBattle:1018 against `struckOnce`, which is per CREATURE and is added by any fromSkill hit (:1196). So the innate punishes the first thing you do to an enemy and pays every repetition — which is a trade no shared skill is built to collect, because the catalogue's heavy hitters (BLOW, DRINK) fire once every six beats and spend most of their casts on a fresh creature. SLOW FALL lands hit after hit on the SAME creature on its own clock, without ever taking a beat: the first stone is 15% smaller, and every stone after it is 59% larger than that first one. It also leaves the Tower's Active slot free, so the innate's penalty is paid once by the field and the bonus is collected by everything else. On any other champion the stones are flat and this is simply a slow single-target field.

variations.name: COURSES
variations.line: The stones fall every 1.5s, each half as heavy.
variations.dials: IntervalMs 3000 → 1500 (the per-second BasePower is scaled by the interval at :1642, so damage per second is unchanged and only the HIT COUNT doubles)

reinforcements.name: DRYSTONE
reinforcements.line: The stones fall every 1s.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt — and it genuinely can go either way against flat armour (:1180 subtracts per hit), which is the trade this branch is. Worthless to KEYSTONE, whose purchase is one stone heavy enough to ignore armour entirely.

reinforcements.name: MORTARED
reinforcements.line: Each stone lands 35% harder.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt on every tick, and it is what lifts the fast branch's small stones back above the armour line.

reinforcements.name: PLUMBLINE
reinforcements.line: A stone hits an enemy under 45% health 55% harder.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt and creatures killed: a fast stream is the only thing that lands often enough to catch a creature inside the window. On a six-second clock the window is usually skipped entirely.

variations.name: KEYSTONE
variations.line: One stone every 6s, on the two enemies in front, and it ignores defence.
variations.dials: IntervalMs 3000 → 6000, TargetsBonus 0 → 1 (SoloBattle:1644, shape.TargetsFor(def) + def.TargetsBonus), DefenceIgnore true — NEW READ SITE for an existing dial: the Field damage path's LandSpread (:1644) must pass `ignoresArmour: def.DefenceIgnore`, which the cast path already does at :1976

reinforcements.name: CAPSTONE
reinforcements.line: The stone falls on the three enemies in front.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt across a wide wave. Structurally dead on COURSES, which stays on the front enemy — and a wider fall would destroy that branch's whole premise, since a second creature is a fresh first hit at 0.85.

reinforcements.name: DEAD DROP
reinforcements.line: The stone lands 50% harder.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt per stone, on a branch whose entire weight is in the single hit.

reinforcements.name: BEDDING IN
reinforcements.line: The stone falls every 4s instead of every 6s.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt: at 6s a short wave sees one stone and a long one sees two, so this is the difference between one arrival and three. Worthless to COURSES, which is already at 1.5s.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "strike", FxKey "strike" — fx_tower_strike_strip8_512 exists. It must NOT play a champion clip (design §8 Law 1: a passive never touches the animation channel). Anchor the effect above the target and let it fall: the strip plays top-down onto the creature's head anchor while the champion keeps swinging normally, and a short dust ring at the creature's feet on landing sells that the champion did not do it.

signatures.name: LAST ARROW
signatures.fantasy: The shot you were saving. It is expensive, it finishes things, and finishing things is how you get it back.
signatures.baseMechanic: Three arrows into one enemy, every 6 beats. Each lands 110% harder on an enemy under 40% health.
signatures.dials: Beats 6 (SoloBattle:1661 — the longest cooldown in the game, tied with BLOW and DRINK), Targets 1, HitsPerTarget 3 (:1322-1341, :1977), BasePower 195 (:1818), Rules.BonusUnderHealth 0.40 and Rules.BonusUnderHealthAmount 1.10 (:1309-1310, read PER HIT at :1331, so the third arrow reads the health the first two took away).
signatures.whyItFits: "Counts arrows the way other people count breaths." A quiver holds a finite number of expensive shots, and this is the most expensive one the game allows. The finishing rule inside the cast is the arrow-counting made mechanical: three arrows, and the last one is worth the most because of what the first two did.
signatures.innateInteraction: LOOSE AGAIN is read at SoloBattle:1251-1256: on ANY kill, every slot's ReadyAt and ReadyAtBeat are written to 0 — every skill is ready at once. That is worth nothing without kills, and worth the most on the longest cooldown you own, because a six-beat skill is the only one whose reset you can actually feel. Today the Quiver's innate has no partner: nothing in the catalogue is built to make the kill that triggers it. LAST ARROW is the trigger, and the trigger's payoff is the arrow itself — the cast is engineered to END in a death (the third arrow reads the target at 110% against the health the first two removed), and that death hands the whole rotation back including this skill. The innate is the reset; the signature is the thing that fires it. On any other champion it is a six-beat skill that lands twice a wave and nothing happens when it kills.

variations.name: CHAIN SHOT
variations.line: Five arrows, no finishing bonus — but when the target dies the rest drive into the next enemy.
variations.dials: HitsPerTarget 3 → 5, Rules.RetargetOnDeath true (SoloBattle:1305, :1343), Rules.BonusUnderHealth 0.40 → 0 and BonusUnderHealthAmount 1.10 → 0

reinforcements.name: FULL DRAW
reinforcements.line: Seven arrows instead of five.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt and creatures killed — more arrows means more chances for the chain at :1343 to carry. Structurally dead on BODKIN, which has HitsPerTarget 1.

reinforcements.name: LOOSE SHEAF
reinforcements.line: Against a thin wave the arrows double up: never fewer than 8 in all.
reinforcements.liveness: Damage dealt against a one-creature wave — the boss case, and the case the chain cannot help with. Worthless to BODKIN, whose branch is one heavy arrow that pays armour once; eight of them would be the opposite skill.

reinforcements.name: RUNNING SHOT
reinforcements.line: The volley opens on two enemies instead of one.
reinforcements.liveness: Targets struck and damage dealt — five arrows into each of two creatures, with the chain running from either. Structurally against BODKIN's identity, which is one arrow at one target.

variations.name: BODKIN
variations.line: One arrow instead of three, at triple weight, and the finishing bonus doubles.

signatures.name: NARROWS
signatures.fantasy: Whatever it hit you with, the wall answers with the same thing it always answers with.
signatures.baseMechanic: Every bite is answered with a fixed hit on the enemy in front. Rearms every 2.5s.
signatures.dials: Kind Reaction with On = Bitten (SoloBattle:2247 — the only event the fight dispatches), RearmMs 2500 (:2251, floored at 1000), ReflectFraction 0 and BasePower 165, which is what makes :2372-2374 take the `PoweredBase(sk.Def, resonance)` limb instead of the `basis * reflect` limb. signatures.whyItFits: "Stands where the road narrows, and lets it narrow further." A wall does not answer proportionally. The catalogue has one Reaction that reflects (JAWS) and one that prevents (IRON); it has none that simply pays its own number, and that shape is the Thornwall's alone.
signatures.innateInteraction: This is the sharpest arithmetic in the ten, and it is a genuine conflict inside the champion's own card. REPRISAL is FlatDamageReduction 6 and DamageTaken 0.90 (SoloBattle:2201, :2224) — both applied BEFORE `attempted` is measured at :2230 — and every reflect in the game is a share of `attempted` (:2371). So the Thornwall's own mitigation shrinks every reflect it owns; the champion whose card says "every trap you set does more" is the champion whose traps have the least to reflect, and against a Swarm of small nibblers the flat 6 can erase the basis entirely. NARROWS is the SNARE answer whose size does not read the bite at all. It pays its own BasePower, which the innate's third clause — StylePower[Snare] 1.35, read at :1003 — then lifts by 35%. The passive takes the bite away; the signature does not need it. On any other champion this is a flat trap with no multiplier behind it.

signatures.name: WITNESS
signatures.fantasy: You call in every promise you have made at once, and each one pays.
signatures.baseMechanic: Heavy damage to one target, +35% for each Vow you have sworn; heals you 10% of what it deals.
signatures.dials: Beats 5 (SoloBattle:1661), Targets 1, BasePower 240 (:1818), Lifesteal 0.10 (:2043-2049, through Heal so the per-wave ceiling and BLOOD MAGIC still hold). NEW PowerPerVowSworn 0.35 — read ONCE, in Amp() beside TITHE (SoloBattle:954): `if (skillDef?.PowerPerVowSworn > 0f) m *= 1f + skillDef.PowerPerVowSworn * swornVows;`, with the existing `swornVows` hoist at :652 widened from `tithe > 0f` to also fire when a woven skill carries the dial. DistinctVows (:2534) already decides what "wearing a Vow twice" means, so the count cannot be double-billed.
signatures.whyItFits: The only champion in the roster built around a SYSTEM rather than a branch, and the only one whose unlock quest is about Vows. Its signature has to be the skill that is worthless to a hunter who has promised nothing — which is the same price the passive already charges, paid in a different currency.
signatures.innateInteraction: TWICE SWORN's first clause is VowPowerMultiplier 1.5, and SoloBattle:2554-2559 is explicit about what that does: it scales a Vow's BONUS, not the factor, so it pays nothing at all unless a Vow's demand is currently MET (Vows.IsActive at :2552), and it pays nothing extra for swearing a SECOND Vow — a Vow's multiplier is per-skill, so four skills at x1.33 is still x1.33. The innate therefore rewards keeping ONE promise well and is completely indifferent to how many you make. WITNESS asks the opposite question: it reads the COUNT of distinct Vows sworn and does not care whether their demands are met this wave. So the champion's two halves now pull against each other in a way the player can act on — deepen one kept promise, or make three you may break. That is a build decision, not a second copy of the passive.

signatures.name: PICKINGS
signatures.fantasy: Everything you have taken out of this place is hanging off you, and you swing it.
signatures.baseMechanic: Four hits across the wave, and they land harder the richer your haul.
signatures.dials: Beats 5 (SoloBattle:1661), Targets 4 (:1940), BasePower 175 (:1818). NEW HaulToPower 0.45 — read ONCE, in Amp() immediately beside HOARDER (SoloBattle:1009-1010): `if (skillDef?.HaulToPower > 0f) m *= 1f + skillDef.HaulToPower * MathF.Max(0f, mods.Haul - 1f);`, the same shape and the same guard the keystone already uses, so a hunter with no haul bonus pays and gains exactly nothing.
signatures.whyItFits: "Fights for the pockets, not the glory." THE MAGPIE is the one champion in the roster whose passive does nothing at all inside a fight — FULL POCKETS is Mods(1,1,1, Haul 1.35, Rarity 1.20) and not one of those numbers is read by SoloBattle. Its signature has to be the door between the two halves of the game, or the character has no combat identity to give one.
signatures.innateInteraction: It does not give more loot — that IS the innate, and duplicating it would be the §5 failure exactly. It SPENDS the loot the innate already gives. FULL POCKETS multiplies mods.Haul by 1.35 before anything else is worn, so PICKINGS opens at +16% on every hit with no gear at all, and from there every haul affix, every Warren rung, every WaveBonus and the whole AVARICE road the Magpie already cheapens starts appearing in the damage number instead of only in the bag. That is a real, and deliberately dangerous, coupling: the Magpie is the only champion for whom the economy screen is a damage screen. On any other champion the dial reads a haul near 1 and pays nothing.

signatures.presentation: ClipKey "strike", FxKey "strike" — fx_magpie_strike_strip8_512 exists. The hits should read as thrown junk rather than as a weapon: coins, rings, the contents of the bag. The effect's scale should visibly track the haul multiplier (bigger the richer the run is), which is the only honest way to show a dial the player earns on a completely different screen.

newDials: SkillDef.AmplifyPerSkillUsed (float, default 0) — SEEKER / EVERY ROAD. Read at ONE site: the SIGN cast branch in SoloBattle, immediately after ampBonus is assigned (~:1749), as `ampBonus += def.AmplifyPerSkillUsed * Math.Max(0, activated.Count - 1)`. `activated` is an existing wave-local HashSet (:725) already fed by casts (:1704) and Field pulses (:1490).

SkillDef.DamagePerDeadEnemy (float, default 0) — CHORUS / GRAVE SONG. Read at ONE site: inside Amp(), immediately after the SWARMBANE line (SoloBattle:1029), as `m *= 1f + skillDef.DamagePerDeadEnemy * deadThisWave`. `deadThisWave` is an existing wave-local counter (:714, incremented :1229). One site covers the aura, cast and trap paths because all three go through Amp().

SkillDef.SkillRateBonus (float, default 0) — METRONOME / CADENCE. Hoisted once from the woven skills beside the existing bleedRate / swingIgnoresArmour hoists (SoloBattle:749-768), then read at ONE site: as one extra factor in RateNow() (:856). RateNow is already the single place every cadence in the fight is asked for.

SkillDef.ShieldPerPulse (float, default 0) — UNBROKEN / HOLD FAST. Read at ONE new site in the Field block, immediately after the Aura event is emitted (SoloBattle:1486-1490): grant through the existing GrantShield helper (:820) and `continue`. The same branch also reads the EXISTING HealPerPulse, which today is only reachable inside the attack-break limb (:1603) — see notes.

SkillDef.PowerPerVowSworn (float, default 0) — OATHBOUND / WITNESS. Read at ONE site: inside Amp(), beside the TITHE line (SoloBattle:954), as `m *= 1f + skillDef.PowerPerVowSworn * swornVows`. Requires widening the existing `swornVows` hoist (:652) from `tithe > 0f` to also fire when a woven skill carries the dial; DistinctVows (:2534) stays the single definition of the count.

SkillDef.HaulToPower (float, default 0) — MAGPIE / PICKINGS. Read at ONE site: inside Amp(), immediately after HOARDER (SoloBattle:1009-1010), as `m *= 1f + skillDef.HaulToPower * MathF.Max(0f, mods.Haul - 1f)` — the same shape and the same zero-guard the keystone already uses.
notes: SIX new dials, and no new engine. Four of the six land inside Amp(), which is already the one funnel every damaging path in the fight passes through, so they cost four lines in one method. The other two are a hoist-plus-one-term in RateNow() and one branch in the Field block. Every dial is zero at the base line of all twenty-two other skills, so an unwoven signature contributes nothing and cannot rot into the dormant state this codebase keeps rediscovering.

TWO read-site extensions of EXISTING dials, which are cheaper than new dials but must be listed because they change behaviour for skills that already carry them. (1) HealPerPulse is currently reachable ONLY inside the `AttackBreakPerTick > 0f` limb (SoloBattle:1603), so a Field cannot heal without also carrying an attack break; HOLD FAST / DEEP ROOTS needs it at the new ShieldPerPulse site. No shared skill is affected — WILT/SUP is the only carrier and it keeps its attack break. (2) DefenceIgnore is passed as `ignoresArmour` only on the cast path (:1976); the Field damage path's LandSpread (:1644) must pass it too for SLOW FALL / KEYSTONE. No shared Field sets DefenceIgnore, so nothing existing changes.

THE BEAT CEILING IS RESPECTED, and it is a real test. `test_the_worst_pair_still_leaves_the_swing_most_of_the_beats` (skill_slot_kinds_test.cs:145) takes the two SHORTEST actives in the whole catalogue and demands BeatDemand < 0.5. SPRAY is 4. Every signature Active here is 5 or 6 beats, so the worst pair stays 1/4 + 1/5 = 0.45. A signature Active at 4 beats would have made it exactly 0.50 and failed the build. Five of the ten are Actives (EVERY ROAD 5, OVERFALL 6, LAST ARROW 6, WITNESS 5, PICKINGS 5); four are Fields and one is a Reaction, none of which cost a beat.

CooldownMultiplier IS NOT READ ON THE ACTIVE PATH. An Active's cadence is `sk.Def.Beats` (SoloBattle:1661) and CooldownMultiplier only appears in the Reaction re-arm at :2251. So "comes back sooner" is available to NARROWS and to nothing else here, and no signature Active offers it. This is worth pinning with a test — it is exactly the kind of dial-with-no-consumer this refactor exists to prevent.

ReactionOn.Kill IS NOT DISPATCHED. SoloBattle:2247 only answers `ReactionOn.Bitten`; WEEP's kill behaviour comes from the BleedOnKillFraction scan at :1233-1246, not from its declared `On`. NARROWS is therefore the only Reaction in the ten and it is On = Bitten. Nothing here declares Kill, LowHealth or WaveStart — three enum members that remain read by nothing.

THE STYLE-OWNERSHIP TEST WILL NEED SCOPING, and it should be scoped rather than deleted. `test_every_style_owns_exactly_one_active_and_one_passive` (skill_catalogue_test.cs:37) asserts `Assert.Equal(12, SkillCatalogue.All.Count)` and one Active + one Passive per style. With ten signatures the catalogue is 22. The honest amendment is to run that test over the SHARED skills only (`OwnerCharacterId is null`) — the invariant it protects is about what MASTERY can teach, and D1 makes ownership the field that expresses it. `ActiveOf`/`PassiveOf` (SkillCatalogue:761-764) must filter the same way or they will start returning a character's exclusive skill.

THE NAME-UNIQUENESS TEST IS A HARD GATE and I authored against it. `test_every_name_in_the_catalogue_is_unique` asserts `12 * (1 + 2 + 6)` = 108 unique names; this adds 10 + 20 + 60 = 90, for 198. Every name here was checked against the existing 108 and against every other new name. None starts with "THE " and none is a style word (both also asserted, :198-205). The count assertion becomes `22 * 9`.

THE LIVENESS FIXTURES COMPOSE WITH `character: null` (reinforcement_liveness_test.cs:81, BuildComposer.Compose). That is deliberate on my part: NOT ONE of the sixty reinforcements needs its owner's innate to move a number. Every liveness claim above is written against the fixture's own five channels — dealt, healed, shielded, kept, reached (Outcome, :100) — with the innate absent. The interaction is what makes the skill CHARACTERFUL; the dial is what makes it live. If the fixture is later taught to pass the owning character, nothing here changes.

THE FIXTURE STILL NEEDS ONE REPAIR to run these at all: `Build()` names skills by id and composes with `character: null`, and an exclusive skill must be equippable by its owner. Either Compose gains the owning character for these rows, or the ownership check lives above Compose. This is the "fixtures accuse the content" trap in its usual shape — a signature that measures as dormant because the bench cannot equip it would be the bench reporting on itself.

REINFORCEMENT ORTHOGONALITY IS STRUCTURAL IN ROUGHLY TWO THIRDS OF CASES AND ARGUED IN THE REST, and I would rather say so than claim otherwise. Structural means the sibling variation sets the dial the reinforcement turns to zero or one, so the purchase provably does nothing there — CLEAN SLATE (needs AmplifyHits), SCREE and CUT PURSE (need hitsPerTarget > 1), REDOUBT (needs WaveStartShieldFraction), WELLSPRING and OVERFLOW (need HealPerPulse), MERCY and BARBED and PICKED CLEAN (need BonusUnderHealth), DIRGE (needs DamagePerDeadEnemy), DRIVING (needs SkillRateBonus), LAMENT/MOURNING/CHOIR (need SlowFraction), FULL DRAW and SECOND FALL (need HitsPerTarget > 1), CAPSTONE (needs a single-target sibling). Argued means the dial would function on the sibling but would undo that sibling's identity — a faster clock bought on SUBDIVISION against HALF TIME's one heavy pulse, DEAD DROP's weight against a stream built on hit count, HEADSTONE's execute against a wave-wide blow that has already killed everything under the line. Where I could not make it structural I chose the argument that is checkable in a fight rather than a slogan.

WHERE I DELIBERATELY BENT THE §6 MECHANIC-OWNERSHIP TABLE, and why. OVERFALL / LANDSLIDE and PICKINGS / HOARD / WEIGHED DOWN use HitsPerTarget, which the table gives to VOLLEY; LAST ARROW / PASSING SHOT uses BleedFromHits, which is VOLLEY's own and stays on a VOLLEY skill. The table governs the twelve SHARED skills, whose job is to make the six styles legible to a player choosing between them. A signature is not chosen against another style — it is the one skill a character cannot trade away — so a character-exclusive skill borrowing one verb is a different act from a shared skill doing it. I have kept the borrowing to two places and kept every style's HEADLINE verb (defence ignore, reflect, amplify, slow, lifesteal) on its own style throughout. If the reviewer disagrees, LANDSLIDE is the one to cut: SHEER plus a second execute would carry the branch.

ONE PREMISE I COULD NOT DESIGN AROUND, stated rather than hidden. Brief §5's example — "if the Innate alters Overkill, the Signature may create an unusual heavy-hit opportunity" — is the ANVIL, and it works. But the same section's implicit assumption that every innate has an unexploited combat surface is false for THE MAGPIE: FULL POCKETS is Mods(1,1,1,1.35,1.20) and SoloBattle reads neither Haul nor Rarity anywhere except through the HOARDER keystone. There is no interaction to design with, only a channel to open. HaulToPower is that channel, and it is the one place in the ten where the signature had to add a coupling rather than exploit one. It should be balanced with that in mind: it is the only dial here whose strength is set on a screen that is not the fight.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. No signature grants a BuildTrigger, sets an Affinity, or writes a SkillShape — those are the character's channel (CharacterRoster) and the tree's, and a skill that wrote them would be a second producer for a value that already has one. No signature raises OverkillCarry (SoloBattle:1271 takes the max of the shape's and the cast's, so on THE ANVIL it would be arithmetically wasted, and on anyone else it would be a HAMMER reinforcement wearing a character's name). No signature is a Reaction on Kill, because the fight does not dispatch one. And none of the ten restates its innate: five of them (SEEKER, METRONOME, CHORUS, OATHBOUND, THORNWALL) deliberately pay the channel the innate is structurally unable to reach, which is the sharpest form the brief's §5 rule can take.

signatures.name: CROSSROAD
signatures.fantasy: You fight the way you travelled — a little of every road at once, and the more roads you carry the harder each step lands.
signatures.baseMechanic: Strikes three enemies. Deals 30% more damage for each DIFFERENT style woven beside it.
signatures.dials: Beats:5, IntervalMs:0, On:None, Targets:3, BasePower:205, Rules.PowerPerDistinctStyle=0.30f (NEW). Read sites: Beats -> the Active cadence gate (`champ.ReadyAtBeat[i]`, SoloBattle ~:1663); BasePower/Targets -> `SkillCatalogue.PoweredBase` + `LandSpread` in the cast block (~:1800, ~:1975); PowerPerDistinctStyle -> ONE new line in the cast block beside `raw *= firstCast ? shape.FirstCastMultiplier : shape.LaterCastMultiplier` (~:1836), reading `weaveCtx.DistinctStyles`, which `DescribeBuild` already computes once per wave (SoloBattle :2580).
signatures.whyItFits: The starter has no lean, no affinity and the dullest passive in the roster on purpose. CROSSROAD is the only skill in the game that pays for the thing a beginner's loadout actually IS — four unrelated skills picked because they were the four available. It is playable at one style (it is still a 205-power three-target Volley cast) and it gets better exactly as the player learns there are six styles.
signatures.innateInteraction: EVEN HAND is a flat +8% hit size with no condition at all — it is a floor, and a floor cannot be built on. CROSSROAD is the Seeker's only conditional number, and the condition is the SHAPE of the build rather than its size. The innate makes a scattered four-style loadout survivable; the signature makes it correct. Neither can restate the other because the innate cannot be made bigger by anything the player does, and the signature does nothing at all for a mono-style build the innate is equally happy with.

variations.line: Every arrow leaves bleed worth 20% of what it deals.

reinforcements.name: SLOW RAIN
reinforcements.line: The bleed pays out two and a half times as fast.

signatures.name: HARDFACE
signatures.fantasy: You do not chase the wave. You set it on the anvil, and every one you flatten leaves the next one softer.
signatures.baseMechanic: Heavy damage to one target. Every enemy it kills strips 12 defence from every survivor for the rest of the wave, down to -48.
signatures.dials: Beats:6, IntervalMs:0, On:None, Targets:1, BasePower:470, DefenceBreakFloor = -48f, Rules.DefenceBreakOnKill = 12f (NEW). Read sites: BasePower/Targets -> the cast block (~:1800/:1975); DefenceBreakOnKill -> ONE new line in the on-kill block of `LandOn`, inside the existing `for (var k = 0; k < skills.Count; k++)` scan that already reads `wd.BleedOnKillFraction` (~:1236-1246), walking the living creatures and doing `c.Defense = Math.Max(wd.DefenceBreakFloor, c.Defense - wd.Rules.DefenceBreakOnKill)` — the same mutation PRESS already performs, and it emits the same `BattleEventKind.Break` badge so the player can see it.
signatures.whyItFits: The Anvil hits things until they are a different shape. Its whole structural weakness is a crowd, and its innate refunds a third of the waste — HARDFACE is the other half of the same sentence: what is flattened stays flattened, and the wave the Anvil has been working is measurably softer than the wave it started on. It is the only skill in the game that produces negative armour from an Active rather than from a two-second field tick.
signatures.innateInteraction: DEADWEIGHT is `SkillShape.OverkillCarry = 0.33`, and the fight takes `carry = MathF.Max(shape.OverkillCarry, castCarry)` (SoloBattle ~:1268) — deliberately the LARGER of the two, never the sum. So a signature that carried overkill would be literally redundant on this champion below 0.33 and a rounding error above it; that is a fact about the code, not a taste. HARDFACE therefore uses the innate rather than repeating it: the carried third is the Anvil's kill engine in a crowd, every kill it makes strips armour off everything still standing, and negative armour makes the NEXT carried spill land harder (`armour < 0f` adds `MathF.Min(-armour, dmg)`, ~:1180). The Anvil is the only champion that closes that loop.

signatures.name: LAST VOICE
signatures.fantasy: The charms keep singing after the mouths have stopped — and the last thing standing hears all of them at once.
signatures.baseMechanic: Area damage to every enemy. Against the last enemy standing it deals 150% more.
signatures.dials: Beats:5, IntervalMs:0, On:None, Targets:WholeWave, BasePower:150, Rules.LastEnemyPower = 1.50f (NEW). Read sites: Targets -> `shape.TargetsFor(vdef, vdef.Targets)` in the cast block (~:1966); LastEnemyPower -> ONE new line in `Amp()` directly beside the SWARMBANE read `if (shape.PerCreatureBonus > 0f) m *= 1f + shape.PerCreatureBonus * alive;` (~:1043), as `if (skillDef?.Rule.LastEnemyPower > 0f && alive == 1) m *= 1f + rule.LastEnemyPower;`. `alive` is already the wave's live count at that line.
signatures.whyItFits: The Chorus is the crowd champion, and a crowd champion's honest weakness is the moment the crowd is gone — the boss room, and the last thirty percent of every ordinary wave. LAST VOICE is the one thing in the game shaped like that hole. It is a FIELD skill that does not care about the field being full.
signatures.innateInteraction: MANY MOUTHS is `SkillShape.PerCreatureBonus = 0.05` — read at the same line in `Amp()` and multiplied by `alive`. At five enemies it is +25%; at one it is +5%. LAST VOICE is its exact mirror: nothing while the wave is full, +150% when it is one creature. Together the Chorus's damage curve stops collapsing at the end of every wave, and the crowded wave becomes a real decision — clear the swarm fast and lose the innate's bonus early, or hold the crowd alive and delay the finisher. The signature cannot restate the innate because the two read the SAME variable in opposite directions.

Read: WeakenPerDeadEnemy/Cap -> gathered once per wave from the weave (`weakenPerDead`, ~:713) and applied at the bite as `taken *= MathF.Max(1f - weakenCap, 1f - weakenPerDead * deadThisWave)` (~:2290).

reinforcements.liveness: health-kept on a five-creature band, where the cap is what binds. Hard-locked — inert without WeakenPerDeadEnemy.

signatures.name: DOWNBEAT
signatures.fantasy: The fight has not started yet and three arrows are already in the air.
signatures.baseMechanic: The instant a wave begins, three arrows fly — before the champion's first action exists. Once each wave.
signatures.dials: Beats:0, IntervalMs:0, On:ReactionOn.WaveStart, RearmMs:0, Targets:3, BasePower:240. NEW READ SITE, no new dial: `ReactionOn.WaveStart` is declared at SkillCatalogue.cs:97 and dispatched NOWHERE (audit §1b, field 9). The site is one block in ResolveWave's wave-start setup, immediately after the wave-start shield grants (~:856-862) and before the tick loop, walking `skills` for `Kind == Reaction && On == WaveStart` and calling the existing `LandSpread(SkillCatalogue.PoweredBase(def, resonance) * VowFactor(...), 0, shape.TargetsFor(def) + def.TargetsBonus, sk.Source, def, since, hitsPerTarget: ...)` with an `if (alive == 0) return Kill(0);` after it. It reuses BasePower, Targets, HitsPerTarget, MinimumHits, BleedFromHits, DamageMultiplier and every Rules member LandSpread already reads.
signatures.whyItFits: The Metronome keeps time; the fight is what happens between the beats. DOWNBEAT is the one thing in the game that happens BEFORE the first beat — it is not on the metronome at all, which is exactly the joke the character is built on. It also costs no action, so it fits the passive half of the loadout and leaves the Metronome's active slots for the shared catalogue.
signatures.innateInteraction: FIRST BEAT is two halves: `FreeOpeningCast` waives the 700 ms breath, and `FirstHitMultiplier = 2f` doubles the first hit landed on EACH creature (read at `m *= struckOnce.Contains(against) ? LaterHitMultiplier : FirstHitMultiplier`, ~:1015). DOWNBEAT fires at ms 0, when `struckOnce` is empty by construction — so EVERY one of its arrows is a first hit and every one is doubled, and it is the only skill in the game guaranteed to collect that. The innate's other half then hands the Metronome its first real cast on the very next instant. The innate is about WHEN the champion may act; the signature acts before acting is possible. Neither restates the other.

HARD-LOCKED by the fight's own clock — DOWNBEAT fires at ms 0, when every creature is at full health, so on UPBEAT (one arrow per creature) the condition can never be true in this skill's whole existence.

Because it fires at AtMs 0 the replay places it on the wave banner's own frame, which is free timing nothing else in the game occupies.

signatures.name: HOLDFAST
signatures.fantasy: The bigger the thing in front of you, the less of you it gets to keep.
signatures.baseMechanic: Heavy damage to one target and drinks 20% of it back. Against a boss it deals 120% more.
signatures.dials: Beats:6, IntervalMs:0, On:None, Targets:1, BasePower:300, Lifesteal = 0.20f, Rules.BossPower = 1.20f (NEW). Read sites: Lifesteal -> `Heal((int)MathF.Round(dealt * leech), ms)` after the cast lands (~:2042-2049); BossPower -> ONE new line in `Amp()` beside the SWARMBANE/opening reads (~:1045), as `if (isBoss && skillDef?.Rule.BossPower > 0f) m *= 1f + rule.BossPower;`. `isBoss` is ALREADY a parameter of ResolveWave (SoloBattle :544), already computed by `WaveScaling.IsBossWave` and already passed by SoloExpedition (:276, :341) — and read by nothing at all in the wave body. This design revives a dead parameter rather than adding plumbing.
signatures.whyItFits: "Has been killed. Declined." The Unbroken is the champion built for the wave that would end the run, and every fifth wave is a boss by design — a spike the player can see coming, which is the whole reason `IsBossWave` exists. HOLDFAST is the only skill in the game that knows what a boss is.
signatures.innateInteraction: SECOND WIND grants `BuildTrigger.Undying`: once per EXPEDITION, a killing blow leaves the champion at 1 health (SoloBattle ~:2398). That charge is almost always spent on a boss — it is the only wave with a 2.2x health spike behind it. So the innate is a single free survival of the boss, and HOLDFAST is what the Unbroken does with the wave the innate bought it: the fork is literally "survive the boss" (DRAW DEEP) against "delete it before the charge is needed" (BRACE). The signature does not restate the innate — the innate is a once-per-run refusal to die, the signature is a per-boss multiplier — but it is the only skill that makes the innate's timing into a build decision.

reinforcements.liveness: health-kept and healed: measured against the deep fixtures, where the champion starts at half its pool and the budget is not already full. Hard-locked — BRACE sets Lifesteal to 0.

signatures.name: TOPPLE
signatures.fantasy: Slow to start and impossible to stop — once you are leaning, even your plain swings arrive like masonry.
signatures.baseMechanic: Heavy damage to one target. While it is woven, every basic attack you make lands 70% harder.
signatures.dials: Beats:6, IntervalMs:0, On:None, Targets:1, BasePower:380, Rules.SwingPower = 0.70f (NEW). Read sites: BasePower -> the cast block (~:1800); SwingPower -> gathered ONCE per wave in the existing loop that already reads `SwingIgnoresArmour` and `SwingLifesteal` off the weave (~:797-803), then ONE new factor on the basic-attack line `LandSpread(tuning.AutoAttackDamage * hunter.AutoDamageMultiplier * shape.AutoAttackDamage * (1f + swingPower) * ...)` (~:2113-2117).
signatures.whyItFits: The Tower is the champion whose value is in the hit that REPEATS, and the basic attack is the hit that repeats most — roughly two swings for every cast at a six-beat cadence. Nothing in the game is about the swing: `SwingIgnoresArmour` and `SwingLifesteal` are a third of one reinforcement each and that is the whole of it. TOPPLE is the first skill that makes the champion's own hands the build.
signatures.innateInteraction: MOMENTUM is `FirstHitMultiplier = 0.85f, LaterHitMultiplier = 1.35f`, read at `m *= struckOnce.Contains(against) ? LaterHitMultiplier : FirstHitMultiplier` (~:1015) — and `struckOnce` is only ever ADDED to by skill hits (`if (fromSkill) struckOnce.Add(target)`, ~:1195). The swing does not mark a creature but it does READ the mark, so on any wave where a cast has already landed, every subsequent swing is a LATER hit at +35%. The innate therefore already multiplies the swing more reliably than it multiplies anything else — and there was nothing to multiply. TOPPLE supplies it. Crucially, EVEN HAND-style hit-size bonuses cannot: `Amp()` returns early at `if (skillDef is null) return m;` (~:1006) before `shape.HitSize`, so the swing is invisible to almost every damage node in the game. TOPPLE is the exception, and it is on the one champion whose innate sits on the correct side of that early return.

variations.dials: Rules.SwingPower = 1.40f — the same gather-and-swing read (~:797, ~:2113).

reinforcements.liveness: damage-dealt against armoured bands, where a plain swing otherwise lands for `MinHitFraction` (15%). SOFT LOCK — flagged: it would also help PLUMMET's swing, but PLUMMET's line explicitly gives the swing up, so the card tells the truth about where it belongs.

reinforcements.name: SHEER FACE
reinforcements.line: Half of what the blow wastes past a kill carries into the next enemy.

signatures.whyItFits: "Counts arrows the way other people count breaths." The Quiver's whole card is that a kill costs it nothing. signatures.innateInteraction: LOOSE AGAIN (`BuildTrigger.LooseAgain`) zeroes every entry in `ReadyAt` and `ReadyAtBeat` on any death (~:1250-1256): a kill refunds the champion's ACTION. On the Quiver the two chain — BACKDRAW's volley kills, LOOSE AGAIN hands back the beat, the shared active fires immediately, and that may kill again — and the chain is bounded by BACKDRAW's own 2.5 s re-arm, which is the only thing stopping it. signatures.whyItFits: The Oathbound is the only character in the roster built around a SYSTEM rather than a branch, and the system is the mark. Every other amplifier in the game costs an action — CALL takes a beat, BRAND takes a passive slot's clock. OATHMARK is the only one whose price is being hit, which is exactly the bargain the character's blurb describes, and it is a Reaction so it costs no action at all.
signatures.innateInteraction: TWICE SWORN is `VowPowerMultiplier = 1.5f, AmplifyWindowMultiplier = 1.5f, AmplifyPowerBonus = 0.25f`. The window multiplier is read at `window = (int)(window * shape.AmplifyWindowMultiplier)` and the power bonus at `depth = ampBonus + shape.AmplifyPowerBonus` inside Amp (~:1665, ~:986). So on the Oathbound a 4 s window is really 6 s and a +90% mark is really +115% — and the mark reopens on every bite, so the Oathbound is the only champion who can hold a window open for most of a wave. The innate says how MUCH a mark is worth and how LONG it lasts; the signature says WHEN one opens, which is the one thing the innate has no opinion about. Restating the innate would have meant "+more amplify", and that is precisely the design the code makes pointless: `ampBonus` is one wave-local state, so two amplifiers do not stack — the second simply overwrites the first.

Walks the living creatures and applies `c.Defense = Math.Max(wd.DefenceBreakFloor, c.Defense - wd.Rules.DefenceBreakOnKill)` — the same mutation the PRESS field branch already performs (~:1567) — and emits the existing BattleEventKind.Break badge. ONE read: Amp(), on the line directly after SWARMBANE's `if (shape.PerCreatureBonus > 0f) m *= 1f + shape.PerCreatureBonus * alive;` (~:1043), as `if (alive == 1 && skillDef?.Rule.LastEnemyPower > 0f) m *= 1f + skillDef.Rule.LastEnemyPower;`. `alive` is already the live count at that line.

Gathered once per wave in the loop that already reads SwingIgnoresArmour and SwingLifesteal off the weave (~:797-803, taking the max), then applied as one extra factor on the existing `LandSpread(tuning.AutoAttackDamage * hunter.AutoDamageMultiplier * shape.AutoAttackDamage * ...)` call.
