ONE read: Amp() (~:1045), as `if (isBoss && skillDef?.Rule.BossPower > 0f) m *= 1f + skillDef.Rule.BossPower;`. `isBoss` is ALREADY a ResolveWave parameter (:544), already computed by WaveScaling.IsBossWave and already passed by SoloExpedition (:276, :341) — and currently read by NOTHING in the wave body. This dial revives a dead parameter rather than adding plumbing.

SkillRules.TriggerBelowHealth (float, default 0) — THORNWALL / LAST HEDGE. ONE read: the new ReactionOn.LowHealth dispatch, immediately after `champ.Health -= healthLost` at the bite (~:2333), as the gate `champ.Health < champ.MaxHealth * def.Rule.TriggerBelowHealth`. Reads HEALTH and never shield, the same rule SCARRED (:1878) and ABSORB (:2296) already obey.
notes: THREE NEW DISPATCH SITES, NO NEW DIALS BEHIND THEM — and all three revive enum members the audit found dead. `ReactionOn` has four non-None values and only `Bitten` is dispatched (AUDIT §1b, field 9): `Kill` is declared by WEEP but actually implemented by the BleedOnKillFraction dial scan, and `LowHealth` and `WaveStart` are used by no skill and read by nothing. The ten designs turn all three on: WaveStart (METRONOME/DOWNBEAT) as one block in ResolveWave's wave-start setup after the shield grants (~:856-862); Kill (QUIVER/BACKDRAW and MAGPIE/PICKINGS, sharing one site) as one block inside the existing on-kill section of LandOn (~:1246); LowHealth (THORNWALL/LAST HEDGE) as one block after the bite settles (~:2333). Each is arm-gated by the SAME `champ.ReadyAt` + `CooldownMultiplier` + `RateNow()` arithmetic the Bitten dispatch already runs (~:2250-2265), and each lands through the existing LandSpread/Heal/GrantShield funnels. A fourth change is an EXTENSION rather than a site: the Bitten payout block (~:2360-2390) gains an `Effect == SkillEffect.Amplify` branch for OATHBOUND/OATHMARK, copying the eight lines the Sign cast block already runs — the same Amplify fork the Field branch has carried since P3 (~:1608).

THE ONE ORDERING BUG THIS DESIGN MUST NOT SHIP. The Kill dispatch lives inside LandOn's death block, and LOOSE AGAIN (THE QUIVER's own innate) zeroes every entry in `champ.ReadyAt` and `ReadyAtBeat` on any death, thirty lines further down the same block (~:1250-1256). If BACKDRAW's arm is stamped after that clear it is wiped every time and the skill has no cooldown at all — an infinite volley chain on exactly the champion that owns it. The dispatch must stamp `champ.ReadyAt[idx]` BEFORE the LooseAgain clear, and must hold a re-entry flag (the same shape `staggeredThisBite` already has) so a BACKDRAW kill cannot fire BACKDRAW inside itself. Both are the whole implementation risk of the Kill site; everything else on it is a call to a function that already exists.

THE FORK-LOCK STANDARD I HELD, AND WHERE IT BREAKS. My working rule: every reinforcement must move a dial that is INERT unless its own variation's root dial is set — the standard PLATING, REPRISAL, INTERCEPT, FOUNDATION, BALANCE, PUNCH THROUGH, RIPE and HOLLOW already meet in the shipped catalogue. 44 of the 60 are hard-locked by that test (the sibling zeroes the root, or the dial is arithmetically inert without a partner the sibling does not set). 16 are flagged SOFT in their own `liveness` field. Two families genuinely cannot be locked with the existing vocabulary and I say so rather than pretending: TARGET ECONOMY (MinimumHits, HitsPerTarget, TargetsBonus are never inert on a sibling that also hits things — the shipped SPRAY has exactly this problem with EXTRA STRING) and the HEAL CEILING (Rules.HealCeilingBonus releases any heal in the build, not only its own variation's). I did NOT use a bare DamageMultiplier as a reinforcement anywhere in the sixty — that is the shipped catalogue's weakest pattern (TOLL, DRIVE, PACKED, STOUT, SILT, NOCK, GRUDGE, SPITE, STANDING) and it is the one thing guaranteed to pay on both branches.

THE LIVENESS SUITES WILL NEED THREE MECHANICAL CHANGES BEFORE THEY CAN EVEN RUN THESE. (1) `reinforcement_liveness_test.cs:196` asserts `Assert.Equal(72, ...)` — it becomes 132, and `skill_catalogue_test.cs` asserts `Assert.Equal(12, SkillCatalogue.All.Count)` and `12 * (1 + 2 + 6)` names — 22 and 198. (2) `test_every_style_owns_exactly_one_active_and_one_passive` must be scoped to `OwnerCharacterId is null`; `ActiveOf(Style)`/`PassiveOf(Style)` use `.First(...)` and would start returning signatures. My ten put two extra Actives on Hammer (HARDFACE, TOPPLE), two on Volley (CROSSROAD plus the Reactions), and so on — the invariant is about the SHARED twelve and always was. (3) Both liveness fixtures compose with `character: null`, so a signature would be woven without its owner's innate — and six of the ten are designed against that innate. The fixtures need a `character:` argument keyed to the skill's OwnerCharacterId, or CHORUS's LAST VOICE will be measured on a champion with no MANY MOUTHS and DOWNBEAT with no FIRST BEAT.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DESIGN, AND WHY. No signature is Kind = Field. Six of the twelve shared skills are Fields and between them they occupy every branch the Field path has — StunMs (PIN), DefenceBreakPerTick (PRESS), SlowFraction (MIRE), AttackBreakPerTick (WILT), Effect == Amplify (BRAND) and the plain damage tick — so a seventh Field would have had to reuse one of those and would have been a reskin by construction. That is also why four of the ten are Reactions: three of the four ReactionOn values were dead, so the Reaction kind is where the genuinely unclaimed moments were sitting. The resulting split is six Actives and four Reactions, which suits the 2-active/2-passive loadout §54 makes authoritative: a signature Active competes with the champion's one shared active, and a signature Reaction leaves both actives free.

BEAT DEMAND IS UNMOVED. The catalogue's ceiling note (SkillCatalogue.cs:322-333) puts the worst pair a player can weave at 0.45 and blames a 0.67 pair for the whole slot rework. My six Actives are at 5, 6, 5, 6, 6 and 5 beats; the worst reachable pair is CROSSROAD (5) beside SPRAY (4) at 0.45 — equal to today's worst and not past it — and every other signature pairing is lighter. All six are at or under the `test_no_active_cooldown_outlives_a_wave` limit of 6. None of the four Reactions costs a beat at all.

NAMES ARE CLEAN AGAINST THE EXISTING 108. I checked all 90 new names (10 skills, 20 variations, 60 reinforcements) against every skill, variation and reinforcement name in the catalogue: no duplicates, none starts with "THE " (the champion naming form `test_no_name_is_a_style_name_or_uses_the_champion_form` forbids), and none is a Style word. The near-misses are deliberate and distinct strings: SETTLE STONE vs SETTLE, STANDING TALL vs STANDING, DEEPER BARBS / DEEPER ROOT / DEEPER VOW / DEEPER DRAUGHT, FULL SHEAF / FULL VOICE / FULL BAR / FULL MEASURE, SECOND HEAT / SECOND FALL / SECOND STRING, DEEP POCKET / DEEP VAULT / DEEPROOT.

PRESENTATION COSTS ALMOST NOTHING BECAUSE THE HOOK ALREADY EXISTS. `HuntScreen.FxFor` (:3662-3666) already tries `fx_{Character.Id}_{fxKey}_strip8_512` before falling back to `fx_{fxKey}`, so every signature names an EXISTING shared FxKey (projectile, strike, aura, transformation, trap, mark) as its fallback and its own strip is a pure art task that can land later without a code change and without a missing-asset risk. ClipKey is equally safe: the switch at HuntScreen.cs:1581 has a `default` case covering "strike" and any future key. The one screen rule that is NOT free is TOPPLE's: a swing carries `FromSkill: false` and HuntScreen grades its numeral a size down, which is correct everywhere except on a build where `Rules.SwingPower > 0f` and the swing is the payload.

ONE PLAN DECISION I WANT TO FLAG RATHER THAN DESIGN AROUND. D1 gives SkillDef a trailing `string? OwnerCharacterId = null`, and `tools/check_skill_doc.py` pins only the FIRST line of an authored skill (`new("id", "NAME", Style.X, SkillKind.Y, SkillEffect.W,` newline `"line"`), so all ten signatures author in the ordinary shape and the doc generator keeps working. But the generator regenerates `design/gdd/skill-slots-and-skill-trees.md` §6 from the catalogue, and it will now emit ten skills no shared-mastery road teaches — the doc needs a second section for signatures, or it will read as though the mastery tree owes ten more roads. That is a §18 exemption made visible in the wrong place.

ELEVEN PLAN DECISIONS, ELEVEN HONOURED — no impossibility found. D2's requirement that BLOW stays shared is why the Seeker gets CROSSROAD and the Tower gets TOPPLE rather than either keeping hammer_blow; D3's two-variations-of-three shape is used verbatim ten times with no exception requested; D8's four slots is what makes the 2-active/2-passive split the binding constraint on my Active/Reaction ratio; D11's "a hunter has two shared skills plus a Signature for four slots" is the loadout every one of these ten was costed against.

judges.verdict: Neither panel is shippable whole, but between them there is a shippable ten. PANEL A is the disciplined one: six new dials, four of them landing inside Amp() (the single funnel every damaging path already passes through), no new dispatch sites, and line citations I checked one by one and found accurate to within three lines — its reading of the `if (skillDef is null) return m;` gate at SoloBattle:996 (HitSize behind it at :998, the amplify window above it at :961) and of the Reaction payout's `reflect > 0f ? basis*reflect : PoweredBase(...)` fork at :2372 is exactly right, and its character is "four Fields and a Reaction that cost no beat", which genuinely changes the SHAPE of a loadout rather than its numbers. Its two failures are real and would fail the build: THORNWALL/NARROWS names DamageMultiplier and HitsPerTarget on the Reaction path, and the trap's LandSpread at :2387 passes neither (DamageMultiplier is read only at :1643 and :1904; hitsPerTarget defaults to 1), so five of its eight deltas are dead; and its claim that "NOT ONE of the sixty reinforcements needs its owner's innate" is true but insufficient — the liveness bench composes with VowId null and `EveryRoadWalked()` takes SkillRoad nodes only, so `swornVows` is 0 and `mods.Haul` is 1 in every fixture run, which kills SWORN DEEP and DEEP POCKETS outright. PANEL B is the braver and less careful one: it correctly finds that `isBoss` is a ResolveWave parameter (:544) read by nothing, that `weaveCtx = DescribeBuild(build, hunter)` really is built per wave at :578, that WaveStart/LowHealth/Kill are declared and undispatched, and that LOOSE AGAIN's ReadyAt clear at :1250-1256 sits below the on-kill scan and would wipe a Kill-reaction's own arm — that last catch is the best piece of code-reading in either submission. But B's line numbers drift by up to eighty lines, four of its ten are Reactions (so "something happens when you are hit or when something dies" becomes the house style for nearly half the roster), and TOPPLE's central argument is false: the swing calls LandSpread with skillDef null at :2117, so MOMENTUM's LaterHitMultiplier at :1018 never reaches it — B cites the very gate that refutes it. PANEL C submitted nothing; there is no design to score, and its slot should be filled by re-running the panel rather than by treating the absence as a result. The ship-ready set is A's CHORUS, TOWER, UNBROKEN and ANVIL beside B's ANVIL-or-A's, QUIVER, OATHBOUND and METRONOME, with SEEKER, MAGPIE, THORNWALL and UNBROKEN re-opened.

perSignature.why: A — EVERY ROAD pays for BREADTH via a new AmplifyPerSkillUsed read off `activated` (:725, fed at :1490 and :1704), and the innate argument is verified true and genuinely sharp: EVEN HAND's HitSize sits behind the skillDef gate at :996 so it never touches the swing, while the amplify window at :961 is the only multiplier in the game that does. The in-fight decision is real — you sequence the weave before you sign. Held off 5 only because the base shape is CALL with a counter bolted on, and CROSSROADS/WAYFARING are SPEND and STEADY re-authored.

A — OVERFALL is the brief's own §5 example taken literally and it works: `MathF.Max(shape.OverkillCarry, castCarry)` at :1271 means no signature may usefully RAISE the carry, so this manufactures the overkill instead, and a 430-power blow on five swarm creatures makes the Anvil the only champion collecting four spills at once. Every dial (Targets, HitsPerTarget :1977, MinimumHits :1935, RetargetOnDeath :1305, ExecuteFraction :2000) is read. Not a 5 because the base line is literally BLOW with Targets: WholeWave — the closest thing in the panel to the reskin §6 forbids, rescued only by the arithmetic around it.

A — GRAVE SONG is the best design in either panel. MANY MOUTHS is `PerCreatureBonus * alive` at :1029; this reads `deadThisWave` (:714, :1229) on the very next line, so the two halves of the champion sum to the wave's opening size and the SHAPE of the sum is a player decision: kill the front fast for +140% song and +5% mouths, or hold the crowd for +25% mouths and no song. Two opposed clocks on one wave, one new dial, one read site serving aura/cast/trap alike. KEENING is correct about the slow branch having no `continue` (verified :1557-1581), so the field still deals. Ship it verbatim.

A — CADENCE is honest engineering (one hoist, one term in RateNow() at :856, the single place every cadence is asked for) and the split of the wave with FIRST BEAT — the innate owns the opening, the signature owns everything after — is a clean argument. But the headline clause, 'every skill you own comes back 12% sooner', is word-for-word THE QUIVER's printed passive ('your skills come back 10% sooner', SkillShape.SkillRate 1.10 on the roster card). A signature that restates ANOTHER champion's innate is a milder version of the failure §5 forbids, and the shot itself is a generic single-target damage field.

A — HOLD FAST is the only design in twenty that makes an existing dead-end into a position you can play from. SECOND WIND leaves the champion at Health = 1 (:2399-2411), where every subsequent bite is lethal; AbsorbWithShield (:115, :2293) eats a bite before anything reads Health, so a standing shield is the one resource that converts that refusal into a recovery, and it rebuilds every 2s while you fight. The new ShieldPerPulse read site is one branch in the Field block after the Aura event, through the existing GrantShield (:820), and the honesty about HealPerPulse being trapped inside the `AttackBreakPerTick > 0f` limb (verified) is exactly the kind of disclosure this codebase needs.

A — SLOW FALL is verified correct where B's Tower is verified wrong. The Field damage path calls LandSpread with the def and fromSkill defaulting true, so each stone marks the creature at :1196 and every stone after the first collects LaterHitMultiplier 1.35 at :1018 — this is the only skill in the catalogue that repeats on the SAME creature on its own clock without spending a beat, which is precisely the trade MOMENTUM offers and nothing was built to take. It also leaves the Active slot free so the innate's -15% opener is paid once by the field. The one new read site (DefenceIgnore on the field LandSpread at :1644, which today passes no ignoresArmour) is declared rather than assumed.

A — LAST ARROW correctly identifies that LOOSE AGAIN (:1250-1256, every ReadyAt and ReadyAtBeat to 0 on ANY death) is worth most on the longest cooldown you own and that nothing in the catalogue is currently built to MAKE the kill that triggers it. Engineering the cast to end in a death — three arrows, BonusUnderHealth read per hit at :1331 so the third reads the health the first two removed — is a real rotation identity. Docked one because every verb in it (HitsPerTarget, RetargetOnDeath, BonusUnderHealth, BleedFromHits, MinimumHits) is a shipped VOLLEY dial; it is assembled rather than invented.

A — NARROWS has a 5-grade premise and a broken dial sheet. The premise is verified and excellent: `trapRaw = reflect > 0f ? basis * reflect : PoweredBase(sk.Def, resonance)` at :2372 really does give a Reaction with ReflectFraction 0 its own authored number, and REPRISAL (FlatDamageReduction 6, DamageTaken 0.90, both before `attempted`) really does shrink every reflect the champion owns — a genuine conflict inside one card. But the trap payout reads NEITHER DamageMultiplier (only :1643 and :1904 do) NOR hitsPerTarget (LandSpread at :2387 takes the default of 1), so BRAMBLE's 0.55, CHOKE's 0.65, THORNSET, WIRE and BRIAR PATCH are five dials the fight does not read on this path. Replace the deltas or declare the read sites; the core skill is worth saving.

A — WITNESS asks the one question the innate cannot: TWICE SWORN's VowPowerMultiplier scales a Vow's bonus only while its demand is MET and is indifferent to how many you swear, so reading the COUNT of distinct vows creates a real fork (deepen one kept promise or make three you may break). That is the sharpest §5 answer anywhere in the twenty. But the liveness claim is wrong about the bench: reinforcement_liveness_test's picks are `new(Source.Body, null, SkillId: ...)` — VowId null — so `swornVows` is 0 in every fixture run, PowerPerVowSworn contributes nothing and SWORN DEEP moves no channel at all. The design needs either a fixture that swears a vow or a second clause that pays without one.

A — PICKINGS is right that FULL POCKETS (Mods 1,1,1, Haul 1.35, Rarity 1.20) is read nowhere in SoloBattle except through the HOARDER keystone, and right to say so out loud rather than pretend an interaction exists. HaulToPower copies HOARDER's exact shape and guard at :1009-1010, and 'the only champion whose economy screen is a damage screen' is a genuine identity. Two problems: the fixture's mastery is `EveryRoadWalked()`, which takes SkillRoad nodes ONLY, and the Hunter is bare — so mods.Haul is 1.0, the dial pays 0, and DEEP POCKETS is dead on the bench; and coupling combat power to a number tuned on another screen is the one balance risk in the panel that cannot be measured in a fight.

B — CROSSROAD names a real and impressively-found read: `weaveCtx = DescribeBuild(build, hunter)` genuinely is built once per wave at :578 and genuinely carries DistinctStyles (:2581), so PowerPerDistinctStyle costs one line. And 'the beginner's scattered four-skill loadout made correct' is a true reading of the only champion with Lean = null. But it reads a LOADOUT-SCREEN property: the number is fixed before the wave starts and nothing you do in the fight moves it, so playing the Seeker is the same fight with a bigger multiplier — against A's version, which pays for skills that have ACTED and therefore asks you to sequence. Both variations (bleed, concentrate-and-retarget) are shipped VOLLEY verbs.

B — HARDFACE is the best design B submitted and the one place B beats A on the same character. Every kill strips 12 defence from every survivor for the rest of the wave, floored, using the same `c.Defense = Math.Max(floor, ...)` mutation PRESS already performs (verified settable at WaveModel:159, mutated at :1545) and the same Break badge. The loop with the innate is closed and checkable: DEADWEIGHT's carried third makes the kills, the kills drive armour negative, and negative armour makes the NEXT carried spill land harder (`armour < 0f` adds `MathF.Min(-armour, dmg)` at :1180). No other Active in the game produces negative armour, and no other champion closes that circuit.

B — LAST VOICE finds the same hole A's GRAVE SONG does — the crowd champion collapses in the boss room and in the last third of every wave — and answers it on the same line of Amp() with `alive == 1`. Honest, cheap, and the innate cannot restate it because the two read the same variable in opposite directions. It scores below A's version of the same insight because a binary that fires once per wave is a checkbox where A's `deadThisWave` is a curve the player can steer mid-wave; and FINAL NOTE is admitted soft-locked because CHOIR carries the same bonus.

B — DOWNBEAT is the panel's best joke and it lands: it fires at ms 0, before the champion's first action exists, which means `struckOnce` is empty by construction and every arrow is a doubled first hit under FIRST BEAT (verified — the dispatch passes a def, so Amp reaches :1018). It revives ReactionOn.WaveStart, declared at SkillCatalogue:97 and dispatched nowhere, and it costs a passive slot so both Actives stay free. Docked one for thinness: one volley per wave and then nothing, with UPBEAT/OFFBEAT reaching for the same bleed-and-concentrate pair B used on the Seeker.

B — HOLDFAST is the clearest 'same fight, different number' in either panel. Reviving `isBoss` (a real ResolveWave parameter at :544 that nothing in the wave body reads) is a genuine find, but what it buys is +120% damage on every fifth wave — a multiplier, not a behaviour, on the champion whose entire card is 'Has been killed. Declined.' The Undying-is-spent-on-a-boss argument is timing commentary, not an interaction: nothing about SECOND WIND changes what this skill does. BRACE is DRAIN/GLUT's DamagePerHealth verbatim with a boss rider, and DRAW DEEP is DRINK plus BALM. Replace.

B — TOPPLE's mechanic is genuinely unclaimed (nothing in the game makes the basic attack the payload, and SwingPower reads at one site on :2117) but its stated reason for existing is false. B writes 'the swing does not mark a creature but it does READ the mark' — it does not: the swing calls LandSpread with `null, null` for source and def (:2117), so Amp returns at :996 before struckOnce is read at :1018, and B cites that very gate two sentences later. MOMENTUM therefore pays the swing nothing, and TOPPLE actively moves damage off the skill hits that are the only thing the innate CAN pay. Keep SwingPower; give it to a champion whose innate can reach it.

B — BACKDRAW is the sharpest character read in the panel: LOOSE AGAIN removes cooldowns, so the Quiver's signature is the one shot that never had a cooldown to remove, and the chain (volley kills, innate refunds the beat, the shared Active fires, that kills) is bounded by the one arm the innate cannot clear. It revives ReactionOn.Kill, and B identifies the exact ordering hazard that would break it — the LooseAgain clear at :1250-1256 sits below the on-kill scan, so an arm stamped after it is wiped and the volley becomes infinite on precisely the champion that owns it. Naming the bug before writing the code is what a design document is for.

B — LAST HEDGE revives ReactionOn.LowHealth, declared at SkillCatalogue:96 and read by nothing for the whole of development, and its tension is genuine and self-inflicted in the right way: REPRISAL delays the crossing and multiplies the payout (StylePower[Snare] 1.35), so a Thornwall that mitigates perfectly trips a weak hedge and one that lets the road narrow gets the big one. DEEPROOT is correct that `takenSinceCast` already banks per slot for ANY skill carrying PaysBackDamageTaken (:2309-2316). Docked one because the cost is understated — the new site must duplicate the reflect-growth arithmetic, the ShieldInsteadOfDamage grant and the REPAY window sum — and DEEPROOT is BANKED and REPAY wearing a new trigger.

B — OATHMARK is the cheapest strong design in either panel: no new dial at all, an Effect == Amplify branch added to the Bitten payout, which is the third instance of a fork the loop already carries (the Field path has it at :1608). The identity is exact — every other amplifier costs an action, this one costs blood, which is the bargain the character's blurb describes — and the innate half it engages is the half the roster card literally prints ('Your Marks last longer and hit harder': AmplifyWindowMultiplier 1.5, AmplifyPowerBonus 0.25, both verified read). It is also right that `ampBonus` is one wave-local state, so 'more amplify' would have been the one design the code makes pointless.

B — PICKINGS is honest that FULL POCKETS is settled outside the wave and that no interaction can therefore be designed, only a shared direction, and 'paid twice for every corpse' is a decent fantasy that rides the Kill site QUIVER already pays for. But two things hold it at 3: kill-heal-lifesteal is the most generic sustain shape in the genre and says nothing that could not be said on any champion; and it reuses HealPerPulse — a per-PULSE Field dial with a live carrier in WILT/SUP — to mean 'per kill', which is a second meaning for one dial and exactly the kind of overload the next reader will trip over.

Verified: field damage passes the def through LandSpread, so each stone marks the creature (:1196) and every stone after the first collects MOMENTUM's LaterHitMultiplier 1.35 (:1018). But everything around that one dial is CALL. WAYFARING is STEADY, CROSSROADS is SPEND, and five of six reinforcements are CALL's own renamed — CLEAN SLATE reproduces PERFECT CLAUSE's line word for word, WELL TROD is REDOUBLE, HORIZON is PILLAR, FOUR WINDS is COUNT, OVERLAND is OVERSPEND. One dial's worth of new idea inside an existing skill's whole body.

PANEL A — OVERFALL. Adds zero dials, which is the best thing about it, and the innate reasoning is the strongest in A's set and verified: :1271 takes MathF.Max(shape.OverkillCarry, castCarry), so any carry-raising signature would be arithmetically wasted on this champion, and manufacturing overkill instead is the brief's §5 answered properly. But the base is PULSE with a Hammer label and a bigger number (whole-wave Active, WholeWave targets), and the SHEER branch is BLOW/FLATTEN with two reinforcement lines copied VERBATIM from the shipped catalogue — PLUMB is 'Defence ignore: the blow ignores the target's defence.' and TRUE LINE is 'After the blow, your next basic attack ignores defence too.' HEADSTONE is FINISH. §6 says do not make ten reskins of BLOW; this is one.

PANEL A — GRAVE SONG. The base is the best innate interaction in either panel and it is structurally incapable of restating its own passive: one new dial read on the line after SWARMBANE, off `deadThisWave` (:714/:1229), against MANY MOUTHS reading `alive` on the line above — the sum is the number the wave opened with, so the SHAPE of the clear becomes the decision. One dial, one site, three paths served. The cost is the other half: KEENING is field_mire/NUMB rebuilt from the same dials (SlowFraction, SlowDeepenPerTick, SlowCeiling) with LAMENT=DEEPEN, MOURNING=SEDIMENT, CHOIR=BRIM — and MIRE is already THE CHORUS's own starting skill, so the player would hold the same idea twice. Base and REQUIEM keep; KEENING replace.

PANEL A — CADENCE. The dial is cheap and correct (hoisted beside bleedRate/swingIgnoresArmour at :763-767, one extra factor in RateNow() at :856, which is already the single place every cadence is asked for), and the split against FIRST BEAT is argued honestly — a rate bonus has nothing to accelerate on beat one. But the effect IS another champion's innate stated in the same words: THE QUIVER's LOOSE AGAIN card reads 'your skills come back 10% sooner' and its Shape sets SkillRate = 1.10f. A signature whose sentence is already printed on a different character's card blurs the roster the brief's §4 exists to preserve. HALF TIME is PULSE again, and the base Field is MIRE minus the slow.

PANEL A — HOLD FAST. It opens the one genuinely empty box — a Field that produces shield rather than damage — on SNARE, where shield is owned, through the existing GrantShield helper (:820) that already caps, emits and reports. The innate pairing is verified and is not a second death save: UNDYING leaves the champion at Health = 1 (:2399-2411) and shield is absorbed before anything reaches the pool, so a standing shield is the only thing in the roster that makes that position survivable. Cost against it: BREASTWORK is BANKED/CARRIED (WaveStartShieldFraction, already produced by both the shape at :829 and a skill at :832) with a bigger number, REDOUBT is more of it, and DEEP ROOTS is SUP's HealPerPulse moved to the new site — half of the six purchases are numbers turned up on dials that already exist.

PANEL A — SLOW FALL. The cheapest real design in the panel: zero new dials, one read-site extension (the Field damage path at :1644 passes no ignoresArmour, verified), and an innate exploit that is exact — MOMENTUM's LaterHitMultiplier reads `struckOnce`, which only a fromSkill hit adds (:1196), so a repeated single-target field is the only thing in the catalogue that collects +35% hit after hit while leaving the Active slot free for the shared catalogue, and the catalogue has no damaging HAMMER field at all (PRESS deals none). Weakness is the fork: COURSES/KEYSTONE is a pure faster-smaller vs slower-bigger cadence trade, and four of six reinforcements are one number turned. Keep the base and the innate reasoning verbatim.

PANEL A — LAST ARROW. Every dial is live and one observation is genuinely good: BonusUnderHealth is read PER HIT inside the hit loop (:1327), so the third arrow reads the health the first two removed, and the innate pairing is correct — LOOSE AGAIN writes every ReadyAt and ReadyAtBeat to 0 on any kill (:1250-1256), which is worth most on the longest cooldown owned. But the dial set is VOLLEY's shipped active recombined: CLUSTER (HitsPerTarget into one body) plus CLEANUP (BonusUnderHealth) plus PUNCH THROUGH (RetargetOnDeath) plus RUPTURE, whose line PASSING SHOT reproduces verbatim ('Your casts leave bleed worth 30% of what they deal.'). A slower, heavier SPRAY is not a signature.

PANEL A — NARROWS. The base idea is right and is a real hole (the trap payout at :2372-2374 does take the PoweredBase limb when ReflectFraction is 0, so a Reaction that pays its own number is expressible), but the design around it names dials the fight does not read on the path it fires from. The Reaction payout computes trapRaw as PoweredBase × VowFactor × first/later-cast and calls LandSpread(trapRaw, ms, shape.TargetsFor(sk.Def), ...) — it never applies DamageMultiplier (read only at :1643 and :1904) and never passes hitsPerTarget (defaults to 1). So BRAMBLE's 0.55, CHOKE's 0.65, THORNSET, WIRE and BRIAR PATCH all move nothing: both variations' weight and three of six reinforcements are dead on arrival and would fail the liveness build immediately. Replace.

PANEL A — WITNESS. The dial is correct and the placement is right (one line in Amp beside TITHE at :954, with the `swornVows` hoist at :652 widened past its `tithe > 0f` guard, and DistinctVows kept as the single definition so a Vow worn four times is still one promise). The innate contrast is real and verified: VowPowerMultiplier scales a Vow's BONUS per skill, so it pays nothing for a second Vow, and counting Vows SWORN is genuinely the opposite question — deepen one kept promise or make three you may break. Against it: the body is DRINK. 'Heavy damage to one target; heals you back a share of it' is DRAIN's shipped active, BLIND BARGAIN is SIPHON plus TRICKLE, and WIDER CUP is BALM's ceiling repair again.

PANEL A — PICKINGS. It is honest about the hardest case in the roster — FULL POCKETS is Mods(1,1,1,1.35,1.20) and SoloBattle reads neither Haul nor Rarity anywhere, so there is no interaction to exploit, only a channel to open, and A says exactly that instead of pretending. The dial copies HOARDER's shape and its zero-guard verbatim (MathF.Max(0f, mods.Haul - 1f), :1006-1007), which is the right precedent. But that also means the game now has TWO producers of 'haul becomes damage', one a keystone and one a skill dial, which is the overlap §1 says must not happen again; and SCAVENGE/HOARD are SPRAY+CLEANUP and CLUSTER once more. The coupling is defensible, the branches are not.

PANEL B — CROSSROAD. The best-sited new rule in either panel: it reads weaveCtx.DistinctStyles, which DescribeBuild already computes once per wave at :2581 and the Vow layer already consumes, so the dial adds one multiplication and computes nothing new. It also answers the starter honestly — pays for the SHAPE of a beginner's four-unrelated-skills loadout rather than its size, is playable at one style, and cannot restate a flat unconditional +8% because a floor has no condition to sharpen. Marked down because both branches are borrowed: FOUR WINDS is BleedFromHits with RUPTURE/SPILLWAY/CARRION renamed, and B ships that identical bleed trio again on the METRONOME and again on the QUIVER; SHORT CUT is CLUSTER plus PUNCH THROUGH. Keep the base mechanic verbatim.

PANEL B — HARDFACE. One new rule, read once inside the on-kill scan that already walks the weave for BleedOnKillFraction (:1236-1246), performing the same Defense mutation PRESS already performs, reusing the existing DefenceBreakFloor dial rather than adding a second, and emitting the Break badge that already exists. No new site, no new plumbing. The innate reasoning is exactly right and verified twice over: the fight takes the LARGER of shape and cast carry at :1271 so more overkill is arithmetically wasted here, and negative armour adds MathF.Min(-armour, dmg) at :1182, so kills that strip armour make the innate's carried spill land harder — the Anvil is the only champion that closes that loop. Cost: SWAGE is BLOW's FINISH + CLEAN CUT wholesale, and BACKING reproduces TRAIL's line verbatim.

PANEL B — LAST VOICE. The one new idea — LastEnemyPower as the exact mirror of MANY MOUTHS, both reading `alive` on adjacent lines in Amp — is good and costs one line. Everything else is field_pulse reproduced. The base is PULSE (Field style, Active, WholeWave, BasePower 150 against PULSE's 140); the CHOIR variation is FIELD/SHARE with SplitPool and SplitMaxWays, and two of its three reinforcements are the shipped lines word for word — NARROW CHOIR is NARROWED ('The pool is split two ways at most, however many enemies are alive.') and EVEN SHARE is BALANCE ('The pool favours the enemies with the most health left, wasting less.') — while FULL VOICE is POOL. The SOLO branch is MIRE/REMNANT's WeakenPerDeadEnemy and cap, near-verbatim. This is a reskin with one good line in it.

PANEL B — DOWNBEAT. It occupies a moment the fight genuinely does not have: ReactionOn.WaveStart is declared at SkillCatalogue.cs:97 and dispatched nowhere (only Bitten is answered, :2249), and the innate collection is airtight by construction — firing at ms 0 means `struckOnce` is empty, so every arrow takes FIRST BEAT's FirstHitMultiplier of 2 (:1018), which nothing else in the game can guarantee. Against it: a whole new dispatch block in the wave-start setup is the panel's second-largest engine cost; the branches are the same bleed trio B already used on the SEEKER (UPBEAT=FOUR WINDS, RUNNING START=SLOW RAIN, HELD OVER=LONG ROAD, whose line is CARRION's verbatim) plus CLUSTER; and REST is thin — at ms 0 nothing is below any threshold, so it pays only from arrows three onward.

PANEL B — HOLDFAST. The single best find across both panels: `isBoss` is a ResolveWave parameter (:544), computed by WaveScaling.IsBossWave and passed by SoloExpedition, and it is read by NOTHING in the wave body — verified, the only three occurrences of the word in 2,597 lines are the two signatures and the pass-through. One line in Amp revives a dead parameter instead of adding plumbing, and 'the champion for the wave that would end the run' is precisely SECOND WIND's own timing turned into a build decision — survive the boss, or delete it before the charge is needed. Marked down only because the body is DRAIN's shipped active in full: BRACE is GLUT with RIPE and SURFEIT renamed, DRAW DEEP is SIPHON with BALM's ceiling and TRICKLE. Keep the base clause and the dial.

PANEL B — TOPPLE. The reasoning is the sharpest in either panel and every step of it checks out: Amp() returns at `if (skillDef is null) return m;` before HitSize, so the basic attack is invisible to nearly every damage node in the game; MOMENTUM's LaterHitMultiplier sits ABOVE that early return and reads `struckOnce`, which the swing reads but never writes (:1196); so a Tower with any cast landed is already swinging at +35% and there was nothing in the catalogue to scale it — SwingIgnoresArmour and SwingLifesteal are a third of one reinforcement each and that is the whole of it. The dial is gathered in the loop that already gathers those two (:763-767) and applied as one factor on the swing line. Cost: PLUMMET is the SAME execute package B already spent on the ANVIL's SWAGE, and the presentation asks for a new HuntScreen rule keyed on the dial.

PANEL B — BACKDRAW. It turns on ReactionOn.Kill, which the audit found declared and dispatched nowhere (WEEP's behaviour is really the BleedOnKillFraction scan), and the chain with LOOSE AGAIN is real. B also names the exact bug the site would ship — LOOSE AGAIN zeroes every ReadyAt entry thirty lines below where the dispatch would stamp its arm (:1250-1256), so an arm stamped after the clear is wiped and the champion that OWNS the skill gets an unbounded volley chain. Naming that before writing the design is the best evidence of real code reading anywhere in the two panels. Against it: the dispatch lives inside LandOn's death block and re-enters LandOn through LandSpread, and one liveness claim is wrong — LOOSE END is called structurally inert on SECOND STRING, but MinimumHits folds into hitsPerTarget whenever `alive < MinimumHits` (:1935), which is exactly the thinned wave a kill-triggered volley fires into, so `pending` is reachable there.

PANEL B — LAST HEDGE. It opens the third dead enum member at the one moment the fight has no reader for — the instant a health line is crossed, sited after the bite settles and before the UNDYING check — and it is on the only champion whose card is about being allowed to be hurt. The innate tension is stated as a decision rather than a synergy and is verified: REPRISAL's FlatDamageReduction 6 and DamageTaken 0.90 are both applied before `attempted` is measured (:2230), so the better the wall holds, the smaller the bite that trips the hedge. Marked down on cost, which is the heaviest in either panel: the dispatch has to re-implement arm-gating, MESH's growth arithmetic and, on DEEPROOT, the whole REPAY bank sum with its window filter and SCARRED bonus at a fourth site. And both branches are SNARE's shipped skills — BLACKTHORN is JAWS/NET+MESH, DEEPROOT is REPAY/BANKED with SCARRED and RAW NERVE renamed.

PANEL B — OATHMARK. No new dial at all — it extends the Bitten payout with an `Effect == SkillEffect.Amplify` fork, the third instance of a fork the loop already carries in the cast block (:1722) and the Field block (:1608), both verified. 'The only amplifier whose price is being hit' is a genuinely unoccupied shape: CALL costs a beat, BRAND costs a passive slot's clock, and this costs neither. The innate arithmetic is exact — AmplifyWindowMultiplier and AmplifyPowerBonus are read at :1665 and :985, so this is the only champion who can hold a window open across most of a wave — and B is right that 'more amplify' was never available as a design, because ampBonus is ONE wave-local state that the second amplifier overwrites. Its two branches are CALL's STEADY and SPEND, exactly as A's SEEKER is, but B pays no new dial for them.

PANEL B — PICKINGS. It repurposes HealPerPulse — documented and consumed as DRAIN/SUP's per-pulse share of maximum health — as an on-kill heal at a second, unrelated site. That is one dial with two meanings, which is the precise failure this codebase has already paid to undo (Undying was split out of the Shield event because one payload carried two meanings). It also has no innate interaction and says so: FULL POCKETS is read entirely outside the wave, so the two 'share a direction' rather than interact, which is the one thing §5 asks for. And its existence is contingent on the QUIVER's Kill dispatch shipping. Branches are SIPHON plus BALM plus TRICKLE, renamed. The kill-into-sustain idea is worth keeping; this expression of it is not.

best: PANEL B — HOLDFAST's base clause and the BossPower dial. Keep verbatim. It costs one line in Amp() and revives `isBoss`, a ResolveWave parameter that WaveScaling computes and SoloExpedition passes and that nothing in 2,597 lines reads. A boss-aware skill is a shape the catalogue does not have, it lands on the champion whose innate is a once-per-run refusal to die on the wave that spikes 2.2x, and it repays existing dead surface instead of adding new surface.

PANEL B — TOPPLE's base clause and the SwingPower dial. Keep verbatim. The basic attack is invisible to nearly every damage node in the game because Amp() returns before HitSize when skillDef is null, yet MOMENTUM's LaterHitMultiplier sits above that return and reads a mark the swing never writes — so the Falling Tower is already swinging at +35% with nothing built to scale it. One dial gathered in a loop that already gathers two just like it, one factor on one line, on the one champion sitting on the right side of that early return.

PANEL B — OATHMARK, whole. Keep verbatim. Zero new dials: it is an `Effect == Amplify` fork on the Bitten payout, the third instance of a fork the cast block and the Field block already carry, reusing every amplify dial and rule that exists. 'The only amplifier whose price is being hit' is genuinely unoccupied, and the observation that ampBonus is one wave-local state — so 'more amplify' could never have been a design — is the reason this cannot restate TWICE SWORN.

PANEL B — HARDFACE's base mechanic and the DefenceBreakOnKill rule. Keep verbatim. One read inside the on-kill scan that already walks the weave, reusing PRESS's mutation, the existing DefenceBreakFloor dial and the existing Break badge; and it answers the brief's own §5 example correctly, because raising the carry on THE ANVIL is arithmetically wasted (the fight takes the max of shape and cast carry) while negative armour makes the innate's carried spill land harder.

PANEL B — CROSSROAD's base mechanic. Keep verbatim. PowerPerDistinctStyle reads DistinctStyles, which DescribeBuild already computes once per wave for the Vow layer, so the dial computes nothing new; and it is the right answer for the one champion with no lean, paying for the shape of a scattered loadout rather than its size — something a flat unconditional +8% can never restate.

PANEL A — SLOW FALL, whole. Keep verbatim. Zero new dials and one honest read-site extension, exploiting a per-creature mark that only skill hits write, on the only champion whose innate punishes the first hit and pays every repetition, filling the catalogue's missing damaging HAMMER field. It is the cheapest design in either panel that is not also a reskin.

PANEL A — GRAVE SONG's base mechanic and the REQUIEM branch. Keep verbatim (replace KEENING). One dial, one line beside SWARMBANE, reading a counter the wave already keeps, producing two opposed clocks on the same wave that cannot restate each other because they read the same quantity in opposite directions — the sharpest innate interaction in either panel.

PANEL A — the ANVIL's and the SEEKER's innate ANALYSIS, even though both skills should be replaced. The proof that raising OverkillCarry is arithmetically wasted on THE ANVIL, and the proof that the amplify window is the only multiplier in the game that reaches the basic swing, are both verified true and should survive into whatever replaces those two skills.
worst: PANEL A — NARROWS must be replaced outright. It names dials the fight does not read on the path it fires from: the Reaction payout builds trapRaw from PoweredBase × VowFactor × first/later-cast and calls LandSpread with the default hitsPerTarget, so DamageMultiplier (read only in the Field and cast blocks) and HitsPerTarget never reach it. Both variations' weight numbers and three of six reinforcements — THORNSET, WIRE, BRIAR PATCH — move nothing at all. The base idea (a Reaction paying its own BasePower instead of a share of the bite) is worth keeping; every number hung on it is not.

PANEL B — LAST VOICE must be replaced. It is field_pulse with a bigger BasePower, and the CHOIR variation is FIELD/SHARE with two of its three reinforcement lines reproduced word for word from NARROWED and BALANCE, while SOLO is MIRE/REMNANT. Salvage only LastEnemyPower, which is one good line, and rebuild the skill around it.

PANEL A — OVERFALL/SHEER must be replaced. The base is PULSE with a Hammer label and SHEER is BLOW/FLATTEN, with PLUMB and TRUE LINE reproducing the shipped FLATTEN and TRAIL lines character for character. §6 forbids exactly this.

PANEL A — EVERY ROAD must be replaced. Both variations and five of six reinforcements are CALL's, with CLEAN SLATE reproducing PERFECT CLAUSE verbatim. Keep AmplifyPerSkillUsed and the swing-reaching insight; discard the body.

PANEL A — CADENCE must be replaced. 'Every skill you own comes back sooner' is THE QUIVER's innate printed on its card and set in its Shape as SkillRate 1.10. A signature that says another champion's passive in the same words damages the roster the brief tells us to preserve.

PANEL B — PICKINGS must be replaced. It gives HealPerPulse a second, unrelated meaning at a second site, which is the dial-overloading this codebase has already paid to undo; it has no innate interaction and admits it; and it cannot ship unless the QUIVER's Kill dispatch ships first.

PANEL B — one of SWAGE and PLUMMET must go. They are the same variation (ExecuteFraction plus OverkillCarry 1.0 with BLOW's BRINK and TWICE renamed) sold twice, on two different champions, in a panel of ten. Likewise A's LAST ARROW is CLUSTER + CLEANUP + PUNCH THROUGH + RUPTURE reassembled and should be rebuilt rather than tuned.

PANEL B — the repeated bleed trio must be cut back to one occurrence. BleedFromHits with a 2.5x BleedRate reinforcement and a BleedCarriesWaves reinforcement appears on the SEEKER, the METRONOME and the QUIVER, with LONG ROAD and HELD OVER both reproducing CARRION's line verbatim. Three characters cannot each own the same purchase.

PANEL C — nothing was submitted. The prompt names three panels and C's JSON is empty, so it cannot be scored, has no design worth keeping and no design to replace. If a third panel exists it must be re-sent; if it does not, the comparison is between two panels and should say so.
